applicability: Applies to parameter objects with a nonempty list of 1-10 distinct integer digits in 0..9 and an integer max_length in 1..4. It counts distinct prime integers obtainable by arranging between 1 and max_length of the supplied digits without repetition, disallowing leading zeros. It rejects malformed or out-of-domain inputs with ValueError. It does not handle repeated digits, digit sets larger than 10, max_length above 4, or non-integer/boolean values.
description: Enumerate all ordered selections of k distinct digits for k from 1 to min(max_length, number of digits). Skip selections with a leading zero. Convert each selection to an integer and test primality by trial division up to the integer square root (6k +/- 1 wheel). Collect primes in a set and return its size as a string. Inputs are validated against the schema: digits must be distinct integers 0-9, max_length an integer 1-4, and booleans are rejected. Uncertainty: the interpretation assumes the count of distinct prime integers formed by arrangements without repetition, with no leading zero, matching the source questions.
